• Review helpfulness is a complex phenomenon that depends on many factors.

(i) the most important features for predicting helpfulness of a review are the review text, the reviewer’s history of helpfulness votes, and the product’s history of helpful votes; (ii) the best performing prediction models are SVM, logistic regression, and neural networks; (iii) the best performing features are unigrams, bigrams, and n-grams, and (iv) the best performing feature selection methods are information gain and Chi-squared.

the field has progressed from a focus on shallow, low-level features to the use of more sophisticated features that capture the semantics of reviews.
